newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mostly firm on crop damage jitters.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mostly firm on crop damage jitters.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mostly firmer amid additional reports of crop damage during a recent freeze in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat growing region, traders said.
Traders Tuesday cited a report circulating on the trading floor that some crop observers had pegged crop losses from the recent freeze at even higher levels than earlier estimated.
But gains in wheat were limited on a technical setback, tied to signals the market was overbought after its recent run to contract highs in the deferred months.
The freeze occured the weekend of April 12-13.

The freeze, plus flooding in the U.S. spring wheat belt and dry weather in key European wheat areas have been boosting wheat futures strongly higher. Traders said there were no surprises in Monday's USDA weekly crop condition report.

USDA Monday said 46 percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop was in good to excellent condition as of Sunday, below the 63 percent in that category the previous week. Also 19 percent of the crop was in the very poor to poor category compared with nine percent in that category the previous week.
Wheat closed 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower to five cents higher, with May up 2-1/4 at $4.41-3/4.

Tenco Inc bought two million bushels of July, Refco Inc bought and sold 700,000 bushels of July, E.D. and F. Man International sold two million July and FIMAT Futurs sold two million July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 20,000 contracts, below the 30,692 traded Monday.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, below the 24,098 traded Monday.
